data.narrative:
Rain Industries is a Seed-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Bryan Hatton, Ephraim Nowak, and Maxwell Brodie. The company has raised $14.7M to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector includes seven private peers (Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and others), though no public comparables exist in this space.

Valuation triangulation relied on one applicable method: Stage-Progression analysis. Using the $14.7M total raised as a value proxy and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions in frontier tech, this method implies a valuation of $37M. A peer-median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Drones & Autonomous universe—while seven sector peers exist, none met the minimum threshold of three filtered datapoints needed for reliable median calibration.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $31M to $42M, with a median point of $37M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer valuation data at comparable stages and the early-stage profile of the target, which typically carries higher variance in outcome scenarios. Additional market data on recent Seed rounds in autonomous systems would refine this estimate materially.
